𝔘.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space. Let $a\in\mathbb N$, $q\in\mathbb R$, $K:X\to X\to\mathbb C$, $\sigma_1,\sigma_2:X\to\mathbb Z$ and $F,G\subseteq X$, and assume $X$ carries a `ProofData a q K σ₁ σ₂ F G` structure (by its docstring, the data common through most of chapters 2–7, except 3). Among other things this structure provides a doubling measure on $X$ with constant $2^a$ (`defaultA a`), a compatible-functions structure giving a type $\Theta(X)$ of continuous functions $X\to\mathbb R$ (by its docstring), and a simple function $Q:X\to\Theta(X)$ (the field `ProofData.Q`). Write $D=2^{\mathfrak c\,a^2}\in\mathbb N$ (`defaultD a`, where $\mathfrak c$ is the project's fixed natural-number constant `𝕔`), $\kappa=2^{-10a}\in\mathbb R$ (`defaultκ a`), $o\in X$ for `cancelPt X` (a chosen point at which every function in $\Theta(X)$ vanishes), and $S\in\mathbb N$ for `defaultS X`, the least natural number $m>0$ such that $-m\le\sigma_1(y)$ and $\sigma_2(y)\le m$ for all $y\in X$ and $F\subseteq B(o,D^m/4)$ and $G\subseteq B(o,D^m/4)$. Assume $X$ carries a tile structure `TileStructure Q D κ S o`. This provides a type $\mathrm{Grid}(X)$ whose elements are (by its docstring) called (dyadic) cubes, each cube $I$ having an underlying set (also written $I\subseteq X$), a scale $s(I)\in\mathbb Z$ and a point $c(I)\in X$, with the partial order $I\le J$ iff ($I\subseteq J$ as sets and $s(I)\le s(J)$); and a finite type $\mathfrak P(X)$ of tiles, each tile $p$ having a cube $\mathcal I(p)\in\mathrm{Grid}(X)$, scale $\mathfrak s(p)=s(\mathcal I(p))$, point $\mathfrak c(p)=c(\mathcal I(p))$ and an element $\mathcal Q(p)\in\Theta(X)$. For $x\in X$, $r\in\mathbb R$ let $d_{x,r}$ be the pseudometric on $\Theta(X)$ that the function-distance structure attaches to $(x,r)$, and write $B_p(\vartheta,l)$ for the open ball of radius $l$ around $\vartheta\in\Theta(X)$ with respect to $d_{\mathfrak c(p),\,D^{\mathfrak s(p)}/4}$. For $l\in\mathbb R$ and a tile $p$ let $\mathrm{smul}(l,p)=(\mathcal I(p),\,B_p(\mathcal Q(p),l))$, an element of the type `TileLike X` $=\mathrm{Grid}(X)\times(\text{sets of }\Theta(X))^{\mathrm{op}}$, compared by the project's partial order on `TileLike X` (by the docstring of `smul`, $\mathrm{smul}(l,p)\le\mathrm{smul}(l',p')$ expresses $lp\lesssim l'p'$). For $k,n,j\in\mathbb N$ let $\mathfrak C_1(k,n,j)=\mathrm{pre}\mathfrak C_1(k,n,j)\setminus\mathrm{pre}\mathfrak C_1(k,n,j+1)$ (`ℭ₁ k n j`), where $\mathrm{pre}\mathfrak C_1(k,n,j)\subseteq\mathfrak P(X)$ is the project's set `preℭ₁ k n j`, and let $\mathfrak U_1(k,n,j)=\{u\in\mathfrak C_1(k,n,j):\ \text{for all }p\in\mathfrak C_1(k,n,j)\text{ with }\mathcal I(u)<\mathcal I(p),\ B_u(\mathcal Q(u),100)\cap B_p(\mathcal Q(p),100)=\emptyset\}$ (`𝔘₁ k n j`). Definition: for natural numbers $k,n,j$, a point $x\in X$ and a tile $m\in\mathfrak P(X)$, $\mathfrak U(k,n,j,x,m)$ is the finite set of tiles $\{u\in\mathfrak U_1(k,n,j):\ x\in\mathcal I(u)\ \text{and}\ \mathrm{smul}(100,u)\le\mathrm{smul}(1,m)\}$, where $x\in\mathcal I(u)$ means $x$ lies in the underlying set of the cube $\mathcal I(u)$. By its docstring, this is the function $\mathfrak U(m)$ used in the proof of Lemma 5.2.8.
